tests: teardown refuses and removes nothing while the shared register names another environment

consumesExternalOutput.program: tiphys spawn and tiphys teardown, over git ls-remote / git fetch / git cat-file / git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: The refusal line embeds git's own stderr through src/exclusion.ts, which spawns git, and SPAWN_GREP matches src/exclusion.ts, src/spawn.ts and src/teardown.ts, so red-witness rule (f) binds this witness. The cited capture is REAL stderr of the shipped `tiphys spawn` and `tiphys teardown`, taken 2026-09-17 on node v26.6.0 with git 2.43.0 against two clones of one fleet home published to a real bare remote. The fixture is the dangerous state itself: environment A acquires the fleet, spawns a scout, and environment B then takes the fleet over with `tiphys lock acquire --take-over`, which advances the register on the remote and cannot touch A's local lease file because `state/` is gitignored and never travels. The named test rebuilds that sequence, substitutes only the four values the capture marks as varying per run (<ENVA>, <ENVB>, <EXPIRES>, <LAB>), and compares the live reason line and exit code byte for byte. The two members separate the decision from its enforcement: member 0 makes src/exclusion.ts accept any environment id as this one, and member 1 makes src/teardown.ts ignore a correct verdict. Under either one the scout worktree, its uncommitted scratch file and its branch are destroyed on a fleet another environment owns, which is the half of criterion 3 that matters: a teardown that refuses after deleting something has failed in the way that counts.
